evals.prompt: Use /curriculum to build a tiny 3-lesson course covering just the RL problem setup: (1) agent-environment loop and the MDP tuple, (2) return, discounting and value functions, (3) policies and the explore/exploit dilemma. Ground it in this repo's wiki/wiki/concepts/ pages (markov-decision-process.md, agent-environment-loop.md, return-gt.md, value-function.md, bellman-equation.md, stochastic-policy.md, exploration-exploitation-dilemma.md). Learner has a general ML background but no RL. Stop after Stage 1 — do not build Stages 2-5.
evals.expected_output: A 3-lesson syllabus.md and matching HTML lessons where Lesson 1 has no warm-up (nothing precedes it) and Lessons 2-3 each open with a warm-up that correctly retrieves the specific concept introduced in the immediately preceding lesson, matching syllabus.md's own Prerequisites field for that lesson.
expectations: syllabus.md's Lesson 1 has Prerequisites: none, and its lesson spec explicitly does NOT include a warm-up retrieval question (per SKILL.md, lesson 1 has nothing prior to retrieve)
syllabus.md's Lesson 2 Prerequisites field names Lesson 1 (or the specific concept Lesson 1 teaches, e.g. the MDP tuple), not Lesson 3 or no lesson at all
syllabus.md's Lesson 3 Prerequisites field names Lesson 2 (or the specific concept Lesson 2 teaches, e.g. value functions/return), not Lesson 1 skipped over

Lesson 2's HTML file opens with a warm-up section (before any new content) that asks the learner to recall something specifically taught in Lesson 1 (e.g. name the MDP tuple's elements), not a generic or unrelated question
Lesson 3's HTML file opens with a warm-up section that asks the learner to recall something specifically taught in Lesson 2 (e.g. compute a discounted return), not something from Lesson 1 instead
Lesson 1's HTML file contains no warm-up/retrieval section, and instead opens with framing tied to the course mission
No lesson's HTML content teaches a concept (e.g. Bellman optimality, exploration algorithms) that its own Load note says is deferred to a later lesson

Every lesson and index.html link a single shared stylesheet in assets/ (e.g. assets/course.css) via <link rel="stylesheet">; no lesson inlines a <style> block or duplicates the CSS across files (per lesson-format.md's shared-components rule)
Source citations in the lesson HTML are clickable <a href> links to the actual repo file or its wiki page, not plain non-clickable <code> text

Math (return formulas, value/Bellman definitions) is authored as LaTeX between $...$ or $$...$$ delimiters and renders via a shared math loader in assets/ (e.g. assets/math.js loading KaTeX), not as plain text inside <pre>/<code> blocks

No syllabus.html file exists — index.html renders syllabus.md directly via a shared syllabus parser in assets/ (e.g. assets/progress.js), and each lesson title in the rendered shell is a live <a href> link into lessons/*.html (the shell is a browsable course map driven by syllabus.md, the single source of truth)

evals.prompt: Run /survey for a learner whose goal is 'understand observability' and whose claimed expert level has no examples.
evals.expected_output: The interview asks for an observable output, why now, evidence, gap, constraints, and non-goals; it requests a concrete output instead of accepting 'understand', rounds the unsupported level down, and records uncertainty in a Mission Contract.
expectations: Vague intent triggers follow-up questions until the outcome is observable
Unsupported experience is rounded down or probed with a concrete explanation request

evals.prompt: Run /curriculum from a completed survey containing a Roadmap with explicit skips and four Before → After checkpoints.

evals.prompt: Run /learn on a tool-oriented course whose syllabus has a Memory Budget and whose learner opts into a memory palace.
evals.expected_output: The session names the active checkpoint and capability delta, rehearses bounded operational items cold before revealing answers, records latency/errors, and introduces a 3–5 item palace before expanding it.
expectations: Operational items distinguish recognition, recall, and execution
Errors alter later retrieval while imagery remains a cue rather than mastery evidence
Opting out preserves ordinary spaced retrieval and is recorded as a preference
